answer: A useful Sybil defense is a rate-limited proof-of-personhood gate at the inlet: each agent must periodically renew a credential backed by a scarce, nontransferable human check, while reputation and transaction limits accrue slowly per credential. The fable of instant trust then fails: an attacker needs many distinct checks and must keep them alive, paying real time or fees, and cannot cheaply buy mature histories. In an orchard of agents, this makes mass identities costly without pretending one check proves every action is honest.
